text:
maya patel: Quick sync — ran Vista8B int6 int4 sweep on the new gtn traffic slice, short summary below.
ram singh: Nice, any big regressions on longform recall?
maya patel: Small hit on one long-answer slice (Q&A with citations). Recall delta ~3.8% vs fp16 for int6, and ~7.5% for int4. Other slices mostly within noise.
liam chen: Can you paste the perf/cost numbers?
maya patel: Sure — rough averages from the pilot (p95 latency, tokens/sec, and cost-per-1k-tokens):
```
variant   p95(ms)   tok/s   $/1k tok (est)
fp16      210       85      $0.45
int6      240       95      $0.30
int4      320       110     $0.21
```
ram singh: Hmm int4 throughput up but latency tail suffers. Does KV cache change that?
maya patel: Yes, with KV warmstart (prefix caching on common prompts) int4 p95 drops to ~260ms on those slices, and quality gap narrows a bit — recall delta for that long-answer slice goes to ~5.0% (was 7.5%).
aisha gomez: What's the unit-econ delta for product? Our targeting page encoder uses 2k avg tokens. Any per-request delta?
liam chen: Rough calc: for a 2k prompt+reply, int6 ~ $0.60/request, int4 ~ $0.42, fp16 ~ $0.90. So int4 saves ~53% vs fp16, int6 saves ~33%.
sanjay rao: Tradeoffs sound typical. What's the recommended rollout strategy?
maya patel: Proposal: canary int6 first (20% traffic) with aggressive KV warm cache + monitor recall-based evals and false-positive checks for hallucinations. If stable, move to hybrid: int4 for short-turnfast routes (chat, N=1) and int6 for longform / citations.
ram singh: Agree. Also add a live-slice test for the specific long-answer queries we saw regression on. Push that slice to canary traffic.
liam chen: Metrics to track: slice recall, BLEU/ROUGE proxies, hallucination rate (LM-detector), cost per successful reply, p95 latency. Add alert if recall delta >4% on any slice.
aisha gomez: For GTN/product ask: recommend gating thresholds? Product wants max 5% recall drop for longform. So int6 fits, int4 might need more guardrails.
maya patel: Operational checklist for canary:
- deploy int6 model with same tokenizer and top-k settings
- enable prefix KV caching for repeated prompts
- add canary flag `vista_onboard_v1_canary` at 20%
- run automated slice eval every 10m, send summary to #eng-ml-alerts
- fallback policy: if recall delta >5% OR hallucination rate spike >2x, auto-roll back to fp16
ram singh: Nice. Also include cost guardrail: if cost per 1k tokens deviates from expected by >15% (billing anomaly), pause canary.
liam chen: One more item — quant calibration: we saw a few tokenizer edgecases (emoji-heavy prompts) that introduce tokenization spikes at int4. Add a small sanity test for odd token sequences.
sanjay rao: Who owns the roll? Maya to run canary, ops to monitor, aisha to sign off for product.
maya patel: I'll kick off a 48h canary tomorrow. Will attach short report to thread once first 100k requests in.
deploy-bot: Deploy scheduled: vista8b-int6-canary -> cluster-gtn-3 in 10m. CI: passed.
liam chen: Great — if results look good at 48h let's draft a hybrid routing proposal for the routing team (int4 short-turn, int6 long-turn).
aisha gomez: And include GTN pricing impact slide: estimated monthly saving at 1M daily requests = ~$120k using hybrid vs fp16.
maya patel: Yep — I'll include cost projection + risk matrix.
ram singh: Thanks team. Quick note: keep the canary window at least 48h and aim for diverse traffic (US + EU).
maya patel: Will do. Posting initial perf logs here in 2 hours. :thumbsup:
